title: Ask the Board of Zoning Appeals for a variance, or appeal a zoning decision
question: I want a variance, or I disagree with the Zoning Administrator's decision. How do I go to the BZA?
office: Board of Zoning Appeals (staffed by Neighborhood Development Services, Zoning Division)
summary: Charlottesville's Board of Zoning Appeals (BZA), five residents appointed by the Circuit Court, grants variances from the Development Code's lot and building standards and hears appeals of the Zoning Administrator's decisions. A variance cannot change a property's use. For a variance, meet Zoning staff first, then file a complete application, plans and fee with Neighborhood Development Services. To appeal, file a notice of appeal stating your grounds within 30 days of the written decision (10 days for some violation notices). The fee is $100/$250 plus notice costs. After published and mailed notice, the BZA holds a public hearing and must decide within 90 days. Its decision can be taken to Charlottesville Circuit Court within 30 days.

steps.step: Pick the right kind of relief: variance, appeal, or another process
steps.who: Property owner, tenant, or a person aggrieved by a zoning decision; NDS Zoning staff can advise
steps.how: Ask for a variance when strict application of a lot or building standard (lot size, shape or area; a building's size, height, area, bulk or location) would unreasonably restrict use of the property. A variance cannot allow a use the district does not permit or change the zoning: a change in use is a Zoning Amendment (rezoning), and a use the district allows only by special use permit needs that permit; both are decided by City Council after Planning Commission review. A variance is only available when the relief cannot be had through a special exception or an administrative modification; staff can decide an Administrative Modification of 15% or less of certain physical dimensional standards (not dwelling units per lot, building height in stories, development bonuses or use standards). Appeal instead when you disagree with a written order, requirement, decision, determination or notice of violation of the Zoning Administrator or another administrative officer. Floodplain variances follow their own section (Development Code § 5.2.13).
steps.quote: An Administrative Modification may be submitted to permit a modification of 15% or less to certain physical dimensional standards per the Charlottesville Development Code.

steps.step: For an appeal: get the decision in writing, or ask the Zoning Administrator for a determination
steps.who: The person seeking a decision; the Zoning Administrator (the Director of Neighborhood Development Services or a designee, NDS Zoning Division)
steps.how: Ask NDS Zoning (through its contact form, by phone or in person) for a written decision or determination on your zoning question; a written request also gives a clear start date for the 90-day response period. If you are not the owner of the property or the owner's agent, the owner must be given written notice of your request within 10 days, by the Zoning Administrator or, if the Administrator directs, by you. A written notice of violation or written order must say that you may have a right to appeal within 30 days, give the appeal fee and say where to get information about filing an appeal. Published determinations are listed on the city's Zoning Determinations page.
steps.deadline: The Zoning Administrator must respond within 90 days of the request unless the requester agrees to a longer period
steps.quote: Make decisions or determinations on zoning matters within the scope of their authority within 90 days of such request.

steps.step: For a variance on a project that needs Development Review: submit the Development Plan or Final Site Plan first
steps.how: New construction, additions, site modifications and some changes of use need Development Review. A project with no public improvements (other than streetscape), no more than two new dwelling units and no other principal use is exempt, as are some site modifications and changes of use (Development Code § 5.2.9.A.2); the city's Development Requirements page gives one- and two-unit homes and minor alterations without public improvements as examples that may go directly to building permit review. If your project needs Development Review, submit a Development Plan or Final Site Plan in the City Permit Portal and receive staff comments or approval before applying for the variance. The variance must then be approved before the Final Site Plan (or a stand-alone Development Plan) is approved.
steps.deadline: Before the variance application is submitted
steps.fee: Separate Development Review fees apply (NDS Fee Schedule)
steps.quote: If a Project is subject to Development Review, an applicant must submit a Development Plan or Final Site Plan application and receive staff comments or notice of approval prior to applying for any discretionary approvals such as an Administrative Modification, Variance, Floodplain Variance, Special Use Permit, Special Exception Permit, or Critical Slopes Special Exception Permit application.

steps.step: For a variance: hold a pre-application conference with the Zoning Administrator
steps.who: Applicant (owner, tenant or authorized agent); NDS Zoning Division
steps.how: Schedule a pre-application conference with the Zoning Administrator (or designee) to go over the procedures, standards and regulations the variance must meet; the Administrator may waive it. Sign the Pre-Application Meeting Acknowledgement (posted as the Preapplication Verification Form) and upload it with the application; the form says the application will not be considered complete without it. The Procedures Manual strongly encourages a community meeting for relief applications. For an appeal, Development Code § 5.2.17 sets no pre-application conference, but Procedures Manual § 3.7.1 lists appeals to the BZA among Relief Review applications and says a pre-application conference must be completed before one is submitted, per Division 34-5.2; ask Zoning whether it expects one, and do not let it run past the 30-day appeal deadline.
steps.quote: Before submitting an application for a Variance, an applicant must schedule a pre-application conference with the Administrator to discuss the procedures, standards, and regulations required for approval.

steps.step: For a variance: file the application, plans and fee with Neighborhood Development Services
steps.who: Property owner, tenant, or a government official, department, board or bureau (or an agent the owner designates)
steps.how: File a complete application form, the required plans and the review fee with the Administrator through NDS, which routes the materials to the BZA (revised plans may not be sent to the board directly). Include the signed Pre-Application Meeting Acknowledgement and a disclosure of the real parties in interest; petitions by owners or their agents must be sworn before a notary and state whether any Planning Commission or City Council member (or a member of their immediate household) has a personal interest. The city also posts a Property Owner Certification (Owner Verification Form), which certifies ownership and designates any agent; ask Zoning whether your filing needs it. No variance checklist is published; because the applicant must prove the variance standard and each criterion by a preponderance of the evidence, ask Zoning at the pre-application conference what the narrative and plans should show. Before accepting the application the city may require proof that delinquent real estate taxes owed to the city are paid (state law also lets it ask about other charges that are liens on the property). Pay in the City Permit Portal; fees are payable to the City Treasurer, and the city does not email invoices for fees except on request.
steps.deadline: On the city's published submittal schedule (no BZA schedule was found)
steps.fee: $100/$250 (BZA – Appeal/Variance) plus mailing costs ($1.00 per owner notice) and the cost of published notice; $500 plus the same costs for an after-the-fact variance
steps.quote: To begin, a complete application form, required plans, and review fees must be filed with the Administrator.

steps.step: For an appeal: file a notice of appeal stating your grounds within 30 days
steps.who: Any person aggrieved, or any city officer, department, board or bureau affected by the decision
steps.how: File a written notice of appeal that specifies the grounds with the Zoning Administrator and with the BZA (both through NDS Zoning). Attaching a copy of the decision helps staff identify it, though no rule requires it. The Zoning Administrator then sends the BZA the record of the decision. An appeal stays proceedings on the decision unless the Zoning Administrator certifies to the board that a stay would cause imminent peril to life or property; then proceedings are stayed only by a restraining order from the BZA or a court of record, on application, with notice to the Zoning Administrator and for good cause shown. Under the Development Code you may contest the certification, and the BZA will immediately decide whether to stay the action. A written order, requirement, decision or determination cannot be changed or reversed by staff after 60 days if the person aggrieved has materially changed position in good faith reliance on it, unless it was obtained through fraud or an administrator's malfeasance; clerical errors may still be corrected with the concurrence of the city's attorney.
steps.deadline: Within 30 days after the decision; 10 days for violation notices and correction orders about temporary or seasonal commercial uses, parking, temporary signs, occupancy requirements in residential zones, and home occupation or office-of-resident regulations in residential zones (Development Code § 5.4.4.B.5). For a notice of violation or written order of the Zoning Administrator, the period does not start until the notice includes the appeal statement and is sent by registered or certified mail with proof of delivery to, or posted at, the owner's last known address (Va. Code § 15.2-2311(A)).
steps.fee: $100/$250 (BZA – Appeal/Variance) plus mailing costs ($1.00 per owner notice) and the cost of published notice; by state law no more than advertising and reasonable costs
steps.quote: The appeal shall be taken within 30 days after the decision appealed from by filing with the zoning administrator, and with the board, a notice of appeal specifying the grounds thereof.

steps.how: NDS checks the application for completeness and tells the applicant if it is incomplete; an incomplete application does not go forward. All filing fees must be paid in full before the application counts as complete. You may withdraw in writing at any time, but no part of the fee is refunded.
steps.deadline: Within 5 days after NDS receives the application
steps.fee: All filing fees, paid in full
steps.quote: Once an application is received, the Administrator has 5 days to review and determine the completeness of an application.

steps.step: Staff report, Planning Commission copy and the case record
steps.who: Zoning Administrator and NDS staff; Planning Commission (variances only)
steps.how: For a variance, the Zoning Administrator writes a staff report and recommendation for the BZA, and a copy of the petition goes to the Planning Commission, which may send a recommendation or appear as a party at the hearing. For an appeal, the Zoning Administrator sends the BZA the record of the decision. Materials given to board members about the case, including a staff report or recommendation, must be made available to the applicant or appellant without cost; the Procedures Manual says the variance staff report is also available for the public to view. Revised application materials are due to NDS at least 30 days before the hearing (later only at the Administrator's discretion). Before the hearing, the applicant, landowner, agent or attorney may not discuss the facts or law of the case with a board member; if such a discussion happens, the party who engaged in it must tell the other party its substance as soon as practicable.
steps.deadline: Case materials to the applicant or appellant no more than three business days after they go to board members; revised materials at least 30 days before the hearing
steps.quote: Any materials relating to a particular case, including a staff recommendation or report furnished to a member of the board, shall be made available without cost to such applicant, appellant or other person aggrieved under § 15.2-2314 , as soon as practicable thereafter, but in no event more than three business days of providing such materials to a member of the board.

steps.who: NDS Zoning, for the BZA (the applicant pays the notice costs)
steps.how: The case is advertised under Va. Code § 15.2-2204 and, for a variance, placed on the agenda of the next regularly scheduled BZA meeting. Notice is published twice in a newspaper of general circulation, and written notice goes to the owners of the property and of all abutting property and property immediately across the street or road (the BZA may use first-class mail). Procedures Manual § 4.1 also says the applicant must supply the Administrator a certification of notice and a list of those notified at least 5 days before the first public hearing, and that notice costs can be invoiced to the applicant; ask Zoning who sends the mailings for a BZA case. Agendas and packets are posted on the city's agenda portal.
steps.deadline: Newspaper notice: the first no more than 28 days and the second no less than five days before the hearing (Va. Code § 15.2-2204(A)); written notice at least five days before the hearing (Procedures Manual § 4.2.1)
steps.fee: Mailing costs ($1.00 per owner notice) plus the cost of published notice (NDS Fee Schedule)
steps.quote: A variance request will be advertised in accordance with Code of Virginia Code 15.2-2204 and placed on the agenda for the next regularly scheduled meeting.

steps.who: Board of Zoning Appeals; the applicant or appellant; the Zoning Administrator; the public
steps.how: The agenda portal lists BZA meetings only when cases are pending; the 2026 agendas read set them at 4:00 pm in City Council Chambers, 605 East Main Street, but check each agenda for the time and place. In an appeal the Zoning Administrator explains the basis of the decision first; the decision is presumed correct, and the appellant must rebut it by a preponderance of the evidence (changing that order is reversible error only if the appellant objects citing Va. Code § 15.2-2309 and the board refuses to reorder the hearing). In a variance case the applicant must prove by a preponderance of the evidence that the request meets the variance standard and each criterion. The board offers the applicant or appellant and city staff an equal amount of time, and at the public hearing persons affected may present their views. Ask the ADA Coordinator for accommodations; the city asks for 48 hours' notice.
steps.quote: At a hearing on an appeal, the administrative officer shall explain the basis for his determination after which the appellant has the burden of proof to rebut such presumption of correctness by a preponderance of the evidence.

steps.how: The BZA may affirm or reverse, wholly or partly, or modify the decision appealed from, or grant or deny the variance; for a variance it makes findings in its order. Reversing a decision or granting a variance takes a majority of the whole board (3 of its 5 members), not just of those present. In granting a variance the BZA may attach conditions and require a guarantee or bond. If an appeal ends in a tie, the matter may be carried over to the next scheduled meeting at the appellant's request. Property with a variance is treated as conforming, but the structure cannot be expanded into an area of the site or part of the structure that would need another variance.
steps.deadline: Within 90 days of the filing of the application or appeal
steps.quote: The board shall fix a reasonable time for the hearing of an application or appeal, give public notice thereof as well as due notice to the parties in interest and make its decision within ninety days of the filing of the application or appeal.

steps.step: After the decision: proceed under the variance, or go to court
steps.who: Applicant or appellant; neighbors, taxpayers or city bodies aggrieved by the decision
steps.how: If the variance is granted, meet its conditions and continue with the Development Plan or Final Site Plan and the building permit. Anyone aggrieved by the decision, including an aggrieved neighbor or taxpayer or a city officer, department, board or bureau, may petition the Charlottesville Circuit Court (see escalation). The 30-day filing deadline is mandatory and jurisdictional.
steps.deadline: Court petition within 30 days after the BZA's final decision
steps.quote: Any person aggrieved by a ruling of the BZA may appeal to the Charlottesville Circuit Court.

escalation.trigger: denied: a written order, requirement, decision, determination or notice of violation of the Zoning Administrator or another administrative officer (including Development Code permit decisions and administrative modifications)
escalation.deadline: 30 days after the decision (10 days for the listed short-term violations); the period does not start until the written notice with the appeal statement has been given
escalation.quote: The appeal shall be taken within 30 days after the decision appealed from by filing with the zoning administrator, and with the board, a notice of appeal specifying the grounds thereof.

escalation.trigger: no_answer: the Zoning Administrator does not decide a request for a decision or determination within 90 days (and the requester did not agree to more time)
escalation.next: Board of Zoning Appeals (the Development Code treats the Administrator's failure to act as an appealable decision)
escalation.deadline: 30 days after the decision is made (City Code § 34-5.2.17(B)(1)); the sources do not say when that period starts for a failure to act
escalation.quote: The Administrator’s failure to act on any process in this Development Code Chapter constitutes a decision, and may be appealed according to the requirements of this Section.

escalation.trigger: denied: a permit or plan is refused because the project does not meet a lot or building dimensional standard, and no special exception or administrative modification can give the relief
escalation.next: Board of Zoning Appeals, by a variance application (a variance can also be granted on appeal)
escalation.quote: to grant upon appeal or original application in specific cases a variance as defined in § 15.2-2201

escalation.trigger: body_silent: the board's vote on an appeal is tied
escalation.next: The same Board of Zoning Appeals at its next scheduled meeting, if the person who filed the appeal asks
escalation.quote: In any appeal taken pursuant to this section, if the board's attempt to reach a decision results in a tie vote, the matter may be carried over until the next scheduled meeting at the request of the person filing the appeal.

escalation.trigger: appeal_denied: the BZA denies the variance or rules against the appellant (or grants relief that a neighbor, taxpayer or city body is aggrieved by)
escalation.next: Charlottesville Circuit Court, by a petition filed with the Clerk of the Circuit Court
escalation.deadline: Petition within 30 days after the BZA's final decision (mandatory and jurisdictional); serve it on all necessary parties and the BZA secretary within 30 days after filing. Filing does not stay the decision unless the court grants a restraining order or injunction.
escalation.basis: Va. Code § 15.2-2314(A), (D); Development Review Procedures Manual § 3.7.3
escalation.quote: Such 30-day filing requirement shall be mandatory and jurisdictional.

escalation.trigger: court_lost: the Circuit Court rules against the petitioner
escalation.deadline: Notice of appeal within 30 days from the date of the final judgment order
escalation.quote: a notice of appeal to the Court of Appeals in any case within the jurisdiction of the court shall be filed within 30 days from the date of any final judgment order, decree, or conviction

caveats: The BZA's own page (https://boards.charlottesville.gov/board/6801) refuses automated readers, so its rules of procedure, meeting calendar, filing deadlines and any application form posted there are not described here. The Development Code says the board sets its own rules, including times for filing appeals and holding hearings (§ 5.1.4.C).

No BZA variance or appeal application form, checklist or guidelines PDF was found on www.charlottesville.gov. The Development Requirements page lists guidelines for other applications only. Whether variance and appeal filings are taken in the City Permit Portal was not confirmed; the portal was not entered (no account). Ask NDS Zoning how to file.

Fee: the schedule's row reads "BZA – Appeal/Variance $100/$250" and does not say which amount applies to which filing (for example appeal versus variance, or residential versus other). The row's approval dates are June 5, 2006/June 16, 2008. Whether the appeal fee meets the state cap (advertising and reasonable costs, Va. Code § 15.2-2311(A)) is not addressed in the sources.

Notice timing: Procedures Manual § 4.3.1 still says newspaper notice runs "once a week for two successive weeks", with the first notice no more than 14 days before. The current Va. Code § 15.2-2204(A) in the index says twice, the first no more than 28 days and the second no less than five days before. Development Code § 5.2.1.B says state law controls. Manual § 4.2.1 says written notice is given by the Planning Commission or the Administrator, while Manual § 4.1 says the applicant must supply a certification of notice and a list of those notified at least 5 days before the first public hearing; who mails BZA notices in practice was not confirmed. Whether a posted sign (Manual § 4.4) is required for BZA cases is not stated.

Development Code § 5.4.4.B.4 refers appeals of violation notices to "5.2.12. Variance"; the appeal procedure is § 5.2.17, so this looks like a cross-reference error. § 5.2.17.B.2 says violation notices must state a 30-day appeal right, while § 5.4.4.B.5 sets 10 days for listed violations (state law allows 10 to 30 days for such short-term recurring violations).

Where to file an appeal: Development Code § 5.2.17.B.1 says "filed with the BZA", while Va. Code § 15.2-2311(A) says with the zoning administrator and with the board. Filing with both, through NDS, meets both texts.

Pre-application conference for appeals: Development Code § 5.2.17 does not require one, but Procedures Manual § 3.7.1 lists Section 34-5.2.17 appeals among Relief Review applications and says a pre-application conference must be completed before a Relief Review application is submitted "per Division 34-5.2", which sets none for appeals. Step s4 tells appellants to ask Zoning and not to let it delay the 30-day deadline.

The Property Owner Certification (Owner Verification Form) is posted with the city's verification forms, but no source cited here says whether a variance or appeal filing needs it, so step 5 tells applicants to ask; the Pre-Application Meeting Acknowledgement, by contrast, says the application will not be considered complete without it.

Local law is quoted from the city's own Development Code PDF (Document Center title "Updated March 23, 2026"; the cover reads "AMENDED | FEBRUARY 17, 2026" and pages are headed "ADOPTED | DECEMBER 18, 2023"). The Municode edition has not been checked. The PDF numbers sections without the chapter prefix (for example 5.2.12); the city's manual writes "Section 34-5.2.12", and the citations here follow that form. Amendments after the PDF was posted were not checked.

Va. Code §§ 15.2-2201 and 15.2-2286 are marked "effective until January 1, 2027" in the index, which holds no successor text. Re-check the variance definition, the 90-day response duty and the short appeal periods on or after January 1, 2027.

No consequence was found if the BZA misses its 90-day decision deadline (Va. Code § 15.2-2312); there is no deemed approval in the sources, and remedies such as mandamus are not covered here. The sources also do not say when the 30-day appeal period starts for an appeal of the Administrator's failure to act.

Re-filing: Va. Code § 15.2-2310 lets a locality bar substantially the same variance application for up to one year. The Development Code read here has such a bar for zoning map amendments, but none was found for variances.

Court steps give the statutory deadlines only. Circuit court filing fees, the Rules of the Supreme Court of Virginia (including Part 5A for the Court of Appeals) and the petition's formal requirements beyond Va. Code § 15.2-2314 were not read. The Court of Appeals rung assumes a § 15.2-2314 petition is a civil matter under § 17.1-405(A)(3).

Meeting schedule: the agenda portal lists BZA meetings only when cases are pending (2025: February 20, May 22, June 26; 2026: March 19, April 16), and the agendas read show 4:00 pm in City Council Chambers, 605 East Main Street. The portal's event records give other addresses for some meetings (610 East Main Street for April 16, 2026, whose agenda says 605 East Main Street; 610 East Market Street and 100 5th Street Northeast for 2025 meetings), so check each agenda. No regular meeting calendar or BZA submittal calendar was found, although Development Code § 5.2.1.C.5 says submittal schedules are published each year.

Asking for a determination: no form or fee for requesting a formal written determination from the Zoning Administrator was found. The fee schedule lists Zoning Compliance Letters ($100 single and two family, $150 multifamily residential, $250 mixed use/commercial), but the sources do not say whether that is the route to an appealable determination.

Floodplain: floodplain variances (Development Code § 5.2.13; $250; the manual names Public Works Engineering as administrator) and appeals of the Floodplain Administrator's determinations (§ 2.9.1) also go to the BZA but have their own criteria and are not modeled in detail. The floodplain page still links older ordinance numbers (34-240, 34-256).

The "3 of its 5 members" figure in step s11 is derived from the five-member board (§ 5.1.4.B.1) and the majority-of-the-membership rule (Va. Code § 15.2-2312); with alternates sitting or seats vacant, ask staff how the count applies.

Privacy: BZA agenda packets and minutes name appellants, staff and board members and give case property addresses, and the circuit court page lists judges, the clerk by name and an individual-looking clerk mailbox. None of these is recorded. The March 19, 2026 BZA packet and minutes were read only to understand the procedure and are not quoted or cited.

Contacts: Zoning publishes no office mailbox, only a FormCenter contact form. The Zoning page gives 605 E Main St as its physical address, while the NDS page lists 610 East Main Street for NDS. Three NDS numbers appear on official pages (434-970-3181 main, 434-970-3182 on the manual and for permit portal help, 434-970-3995 Zoning).

Escalation type: the BZA rungs use "external administrative review" (a board over an administrative officer, per the ladders vocabulary). The building permit file labels the analogous local building appeals board "internal appeal"; a maintainer may want one label for both.
The PDFs listed as forms have no fillable fields (checked for AcroForm and widget annotations), so fillable is false.

corrections: Quotes: all 84 draft quotes confirmed. The 44 state-law quotes are substrings of I.text_of for the cited section (whitespace normalised only) and sit under the cited subsection or subdivision. The 40 local quotes were re-fetched and match word for word: the Development Code PDF (View/16092), the Procedures Manual (View/16093), the Administrative Modification guidelines (View/16168) and the fee schedule (View/11182). The fee rows were checked in the PDF's content-stream order, which gives BZA Appeal/Variance $100/$250 and After the Fact BZA - Variance $500; a column-layout extraction misaligns that table and should not be used to re-check it.

11 quotes added and confirmed the same way (2 state, 9 local): Va. Code § 15.2-2309(1) order of evidence; § 15.2-2311(A) transmittal of the record; Development Code §§ 5.2.17(C)(3)(c), 5.2.11(A)(2) and 5.2.9(A)(2)(a); the Development Requirements FAQ; Procedures Manual §§ 3.7.1, 3.7.3, 4.1 and 4.2.1; the NDS page's invoice notice. 95 quotes now, all confirmed.

s6: the draft applied the rule that the appeal period does not start until the notice is given to every decision. Va. Code § 15.2-2311(A) ties it to a notice of violation or written order with the appeal statement, sent by registered or certified mail with proof of delivery or posted at the owner's last known address. The deadline now says so.

s6: the 60-day rule now matches § 15.2-2311(C). The person must have materially changed position in good faith reliance; the draft said only that they relied on it. The exceptions are fraud or malfeasance, and clerical corrections need the concurrence of the city's attorney.

s6: the stay now includes the restraining-order conditions in § 15.2-2311(B), and the Development Code right to contest the certification (§ 5.2.17(C)(3)(c)). The draft gave 'with a copy of the decision' as part of the filing; no source requires it, so it is now labelled as practical advice.

s2: fixed 'in writing (contact form, phone or in person)', which contradicted itself. The owner notice for a non-owner's request now names who gives it: the Zoning Administrator, or the requester if the Administrator directs (§ 15.2-2204(H)). The notice of violation statement now says 'may have a right to appeal', as § 15.2-2311(A) does.
s3: the Development Review exemption now follows Development Code § 5.2.9(A)(2) and the city's FAQ. Such projects 'may' go directly to building permit review; the draft said they 'usually' do.

s4: the draft said only that the Development Code requires no pre-application conference for appeals. Procedures Manual § 3.7.1 lists § 34-5.2.17 appeals among Relief Review applications and requires a pre-application conference before one is submitted. The step now tells appellants to ask Zoning and not to miss the 30-day deadline over it. The community meeting wording follows the manual, and the acknowledgement form's completeness rule was added.

s5: the draft gave the Property Owner Certification as a required inclusion; no source read says a BZA filing needs it, so the step now tells applicants to ask. The notary requirement is limited to petitions by owners or their agents, and immediate household members are included (§ 5.2.1(C)(2)). Local and state rules on delinquent taxes are told apart: the city code names real estate taxes, and § 15.2-2286(B) allows other liens. A quote was added for the invoice warning.

s8: 'must also be given to you free' changed to 'made available ... without cost' (§ 15.2-2308.1(B)). Added the duty to disclose an ex parte discussion (§ 15.2-2308.1(A)) and the manual's statement that the staff report is public.

s9: 'next regularly scheduled meeting' now applies only to variances, since Manual § 3.7.3 covers variances only. Added Manual § 4.1, under which the applicant must supply a certification of notice and notice costs can be invoiced. The step's 5-day written-notice deadline now has a Manual § 4.2.1 quote behind it.

s10: the meeting time and place are hedged ('check each agenda'), because the portal's event records list other addresses. 'Takes public comment' was replaced by the hearing right ('persons affected may present their views'), and the objection rule for the order of evidence was added (§ 15.2-2309(1)).

s11: findings in the order, conditions and the bond are now limited to variances (Development Code § 5.2.12(C)(3)). Added 'wholly or partly' (§ 15.2-2312) and the precise expansion limit (§ 15.2-2309(2)).
s12: 'including a neighbor' changed to an aggrieved neighbor, taxpayer or city body, as § 15.2-2314(A) requires.
s1: the use limit and the special use permit pointer are now clearer, and the Administrative Modification exclusions from Development Code § 5.2.11(A)(2) were added.

Contacts: 'City Hall' removed from the Zoning address, because the Zoning page does not say it. All other contacts were re-checked on the NDS, Zoning, Development Requirements and Commissions pages, the April 16, 2026 agenda and the Circuit Court page: office lines and office mailboxes only.

Caveats: added the Development Code dates (the cover reads 'AMENDED | FEBRUARY 17, 2026'; the Document Center title says 'Updated March 23, 2026'). Also added the notice-mailing conflict between Manual § 4.1 and § 4.2.1, the meeting addresses in the portal, the property addresses in the packets (privacy), and two new caveats: the pre-application conference for appeals and the owner certification.
open_issues: The BZA's own page and rules were not read: boards.charlottesville.gov robots.txt is 'Disallow: /'. Development Code § 5.1.4.C says the board's rules set times for filing appeals and holding hearings, so a filing deadline or form may exist that this file does not show.

No BZA variance or appeal application form, checklist or Permit Portal application type was found. How a notice of appeal is filed in practice (portal, paper or email) is not confirmed. Steps s5 and s6 tell the reader to ask NDS Zoning.
The fee schedule's '$100/$250' row does not say which amount applies to which filing. Whether the appeal fee stays within the state cap (§ 15.2-2311(A)) is not addressed.

Who sends BZA mailed notices is unclear: Manual § 4.1 (applicant certifies) and § 4.2.1 (the Administrator gives notice) differ. Manual § 4.3.1 still gives the older newspaper timing; current § 15.2-2204(A) controls under Development Code § 5.2.1.B.
Whether a pre-application conference is expected before an appeal is unclear (Manual § 3.7.1 versus Development Code § 5.2.17).

Two short appeal periods conflict. Development Code § 5.4.4(B)(5) sets 10-day periods, but § 5.2.17(B)(2) requires notices to state 30 days. Whether 'Parking', 'Temporary signs' and home occupation violations fit the state's 'similar short-term, recurring violations' (§ 15.2-2286(A)(4)) was not determined.

Municode was not accessed, and amendments after the posted Development Code PDF were not checked. Va. Code §§ 15.2-2201 and 15.2-2286 are marked effective until January 1, 2027, and the index has no successor text.
Circuit Court filing fees, the Rules of the Supreme Court of Virginia (including Part 5A) and any remedy if the BZA misses its 90-day deadline were not researched.
Form f3 (Property Owner Certification) is listed but no step's form field references it (step s5 mentions it in text).
